sentences: Today we're going to talk about something that really happened to you.
I'll go first and then it'll be your turn.
On Saturday I tried to build a bookshelf, but I lost a screw, so it wobbled.
I was quite cross because it took all afternoon.
What happened when you played it?
You saved the game, then it was dinner.
Let me say your story back to you.
You played your new game, Dragon Quest, on the Switch.
You got to level five and lost to a big dragon three times, and you felt really annoyed.
Then you tried again and beat it, and you felt happy.
You saved the game and it was dinner.
Thanks for telling me your story.

labelled_transcript: Therapist. Hi there. Today we're going to talk about something that really happened to you. I'll go first and then it'll be your turn. On Saturday I tried to build a bookshelf, but I lost a screw, so it wobbled. I was quite cross because it took all afternoon. Okay, now it's your turn. Child. My new game. Therapist. Your new game. What's it called? Child. Dragon Quest. It's on the Switch. Therapist. Dragon Quest on the Switch. What happened when you played it? Child. I got to level five. Then a big dragon came. Therapist. A big dragon came. What did you do? Child. I lost. Three times. Therapist. You lost three times. How did that feel? Child. Annoyed. Therapist. Really annoyed. Child. Really annoyed. Therapist. That sounds frustrating. Who were you playing with? Child. The dragon has fire. Therapist. The dragon has fire. And where were you playing? Child. Um. I don't know. Therapist. That's okay. What happened next? Child. I tried again. I beat it. Therapist. You beat the dragon. How did you feel then? Child. Happy. Therapist. Happy. How did it end? Child. I saved it. Then it was dinner. Therapist. You saved the game, then it was dinner. Let me say your story back to you. You played your new game, Dragon Quest, on the Switch. You got to level five and lost to a big dragon three times, and you felt really annoyed. Then you tried again and beat it, and you felt happy. You saved the game and it was dinner. Did I get that right? Child. Yeah. Therapist. Thanks for telling me your story. You did a really great job.

written.summary: The child told about playing Dragon Quest on the Switch and reached level five. A big dragon came and the child lost three times and was really annoyed. The dragon had fire, the child didn't know what to do, tried again, beat the dragon, saved it, and then it was dinner.
goals: Say why they felt that way.
focus: The child will identify the people present in the event.
The child will identify the location of the event.
The child will explain their feelings during the event.
The child will provide a reason for their feelings or actions using 'because' or 'so'.
prompts: How did you feel about that?
Why did you feel that way, because or so?
